Tim David, Rajat Patidar and Devdutt Padikkal put on a marauding batting show to lift RCB to a daunting 250/3. RCB have registered four consecutive triumphs over CSK for the first time in the IPL’s history.

Article Title: Clavicular Viral Controversy: "Trans women are.....": Clavicular’s viral moment with trans women sparks fresh conversation on internet culture
Article Text:
A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Instead of conflict, the exchange highlights shared influence and mutual awareness. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration rather than ownership.

Clavicular and trans women share a surprising realization about online trends







The video of Clavicular, a short-video producer, is going around the Internet, yet not the reason why. There is no yelling or over-the-top drama. It is a mere, everyday talk that seems almost novel nowadays, in the age of internet, which is overflowing with content. The scene is easy-going, the tone of the narrative is straightforward, and the characters appear more concerned with conversation than combat.The message that is being addressed is the flow of the conversation. It discusses internet culture, the way people communicate with one another and the place of trends. Rather than bringing out a debate, the encounter towards curiosity. It quietly brings attention to something that a lot of people who use the internet notice but don't often say out loud. People in different communities often have a bigger impact on each other than they think.The conversation begins with a confident and lighthearted comment from one of the trans women present. She says, "You know that trans women are like the OG lip masters, right? We are very talented in the program. Like, I do the peptides, I'm on Zeta." Her tone carries a mix of pride and humor, setting a relaxed vibe at the table.Clavicular responds in a way that keeps the mood steady but adds a different angle.He says, "That is funny because you guys were using a lot of the words in like the South Korean subreddits in like 2014." It’s not confrontational. If anything, it feels like an observation. He points to how certain words and ideas may have traveled across different online spaces over time.Another voice joins in and brings the moment full circle. "Guys, we're like the OGs. I saw a couple of posts about that. We're like copying each other." That line hits in a simple but honest way. It reflects something familiar. Online culture is rarely created in isolation. It grows through sharing, borrowing, and sometimes even unknowingly repeating.That's what makes the clip so powerful. It doesn't want to make a point or win an argument. It only shows a group of people talking, listening, and figuring something out together.This moment feels different in a space where viral content often leads to fights. It reminds people that conversations can be calm, thoughtful, and still important. And sometimes, that honest silence is what makes it work.
Article Summary: A viral clip featuring Clavicular and trans women is gaining attention for its calm and honest tone. The conversation explores how online language and trends move across communities. Viewers are engaging with its thoughtful nature, as it reflects how internet culture evolves through collaboration.

Article Title: Stuck in driving seat, pulled out from drain too late: How a gym outing turned fatal for 20-year-old US student in Delhi
Article Text:
The accident site where a 20-year-old student, Yashvendra Singh, was killed after his car rammed a tree and plunged into an open drain in south Delhi's Vasant Kunj Friday





NEW DELHI: Business student Yashvendra Singh had come home from US just 10 days ago, looking forward to spending time with his family. Instead, his family and friends stood outside Safdarjung Hospital Saturday, waiting to take home the body of the 20-year-old.They alleged that systemic negligence led to his death. For the woman accompanying Singh, a friend he met at the university, some locals turned out to be angels in disguise — they climbed into the drain and pulled her to safety.An eyewitness, Pradeep, a local RWA president, said, “I came around 6am when two of his friends said ‘please save our friend’. He was stuck in the driving seat and the seat belt would not open. He choked on the drain water.Police removed and rushed him to hospital, but he was dead by then.”Singh was pursuing his business degree at a university in Bloomington, Indiana. While the family moved frequently because of his father’s postings, Singh had completed his schooling from an institution in Chanakyapuri before leaving for higher studies abroad in 2024. During his school years, he was a national-level basketball player and a gold medallist.He is survived by his father, a serving brigadier in Indian Army posted in Kolkata, mother and elder brother, who works in US.Singh’s mother came to the city around a month ago to be with her father, a doctor who runs a hospital in Bareilly and is undergoing treatment for cancer. “We were all so anxious about his grandfather’s health. Little did we know we would be laying his young grandson to rest,” said an uncle from Muzaffarnagar. The grandfather is staying at the Army guesthouse in Delhi Cantonment while receiving treatment, he said.Friends and colleagues of Singh’s father remembered the young man for the promising future ahead of him. “Authorities must examine the circumstances surrounding the incident, particularly in light of repeated similar deaths linked to alleged civic negligence in the city,” a family friend said. His childhood friends also struggled to come to terms with the loss.“Singh was going to the gym with the friend,” the uncle said. Police, however, said they had stayed at a friend’s house the previous night and were going to her place.While Singh’s paternal grandfather lives in Dehradun, the family is originally from Bulandshahr in UttarPradesh.As family members prepared for his final rites, his near and dear ones struggled to reconcile the vibrant young man they remembered with the tragedy. What was meant to be a visit home has left behind a grieving family, heartbroken friends and countless unanswered questions.
Article Summary: Business student Yashvendra Singh, 20, was killed after his car rammed a tree and plunged into an open drain in south Delhi's Vasant Kunj Friday. For the woman accompanying Singh, a friend he met at the university, some locals turned out to be angels in disguise — they climbed into the drain and pulled her to safety.

Article Title: Anna to Delhi via Boston: The ‘cockroach’ who sparked a metamorphosis
Article Text:
Janta Party (CJP) Founder Abhijeet Dipke, with supporters, celebrates after Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and took responsibility for the NEET paper leak. (PTI Photo)

Dalit identity, at front & centre of protest





What if all cockroaches come together?” Abhijeet Dipke posted on X on May 16, while studying in Boston. Dipke, who had participated in an Anna Hazare stir while still in school, was responding to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s courtroom remarks likening some unemployed youngsters to cockroaches.Though the CJI later clarified he had been referring to fake lawyers with fraudulent degrees, Dipke’s satirical post had already captured the frustration of many.Also read: 'If you had not called us 'cockroaches'...': Abhijit Dipke's message to CJI Surya Kant Hours after his post, he announced: “Launching a new platform for all the “cockroaches” out there. If you wish to join, hit the link below. Eligibility criteria: • Unemployed • Lazy • Chronically online • Ability to rant professionally.”That was the birth of Cockroach Janta Party. It didn’t matter that Dipke was over 11,000 km away, completing his Master of Science in Public Relations from Boston University.He was mocked and doubts were raised about the platform, which began almost as a joke. Even a week after the CJP’s formation, there was no clear path. As criticism grew and calls for him intensified to return to India to bring what he started to a logical conclusion, Dipke announced he would come back and hold a demonstration at Jantar Mantar on June 6, demanding Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation.By then, CJP had already made waves, first because its social media handles had gathered millions of followers in a matter of days, and then because its X handle was blocked in India on May 21 over “national security concerns”.Dipke is no stranger to the ways of social media. Born in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (earlier known as Aurangabad), the 30-year-old went to Pune to study engineering but switched to journalism.Dipke’s father Bhagwanrao retired as a deputy engineer in MIDC, mother Anita Dipke, is a homemaker, while his elder sister, Varsha, is based in US. According to the family members, Abhijeet was drawn to public causes as early as Class VIII, during the Anna Hazare movement, when he wore the “Main Anna Hazare” cap during protests.He also started working with Aam Aadmi Party in its social media team, with focus on the youth and Instagram. He rose to become the party’s national social media coordinator and was particularly active in the 2020 Delhi and 2022 Punjab assembly polls before leaving for US in 2023.It was also on social media that Dipke answered questions on social justice and reservation.When a social-media user asked him about his stance on Dalit causes, Dipke replied, “I am a Dalit myself. I hope that will answer all your questions.”And it is his Dalit identity that he kept at the forefront throughout the protest. When he landed at the Delhi airport on the morning of June 6, he walked out holding a copy of My Autobiography – a compilation of Dr B R Ambedkar’s speeches, letters, and writings – above his head.On Saturday, after getting news that Pradhan resigned, Dipke again held up a portrait of Ambedkar, following up “Bharat Mata ki Jai” with a full-throated “Jai Jai Jai Jai Jai Bhim”.Hours after the resignation was announced, he changed his X display picture from that of Sonam Wangchuk’s to the Constitution of India.According to those who knew him during his AAP days, this is not surprising.“He has always been vocal about his identity and social justice. Before he became the face of this movement, he was mostly behind the scenes, pushing out clever memes and posts for AAP that gained traction for the party,” said an AAP member who has worked with Dipke in the past.Memes have been the Cockroach Janta Party’s main firepower.Throughout the protest, CJP has posted tongue-in-cheek, and sometimes cheeky, memes, photos and short videos for its core constituency – Gen Z.After the National Testing Agency announced the termination of services of 47 officials on Friday, Dipke posted a photo of a small fish in a hand.When NCP (SP) national spokesperson Anish Gawande took Dipke to a doctor and posted a photo of Dipke inside a clinic getting a shot for his fever and persistent cough, he replied: “That was more of a stabbing than an injection. You seriously need to change your doctor, Anish. Will be back to Jantar Mantar tonight!” And after CJP spokespersons Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka held a joint press conference with Union ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh, where they announced that the agitation had been withdrawn, Dipke posted: Going to take a nap. See you all in a little while. Jai Hind, Jai Bhim.
Article Summary: Abhijeet Dipke is the founder of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) The party was formed in response to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant's remarks likening unemployed youngsters to cockroaches. Dipke, 30, is a graduate of Boston University with a Master of Science in Public Relations.

Article Title: A new generation of ghazal singers experiments with the old form
Article Text: Poet-academic Kalim Ajiz captured his reason for penning ghazals in a perceptive couplet:Woh jo shairi ka sabab hua woh mamla bhi ajab hua/Main ghazal sunaun hun isliye ke zamana usko bhula na de(The reason for my becoming a poet was a strange incident/ I say ghazals because people should not forget those painful incidents)Whatever the reason Ajiz or any other poet may have for writing ghazals, the fact is people have not forgotten them. Ghazal, the beautiful form of conveying tender, often romantic feelings, have survived the pulls, distractions and short attention span in our times.Keeping the flame of ghazal’s alive among the connoisseurs are a bunch of young singers.Post--legends like Mehdi Hasan Jagjit Singh , Pankaj Udhas, pioneering couple Rajendra and Nina Mehta popular as “Musical Mehta’s”, the torch has been passed over to a bunch of young, energetic ghazal singers.Most of them come from non-Urdu, non-musical backgrounds, yet they have kept the genre alive and flourishing.Take Nihira Joshi. Coming from a traditional Maharashtrian family in Dadar, Joshi first performed solo when she was 16. “It was my urge to express human emotions which attracted me to ghazal singing. Joining legendary musicians Kalyanji-Anandji’s troupe “Little Wonders”, I got a platform which catapulted me to a challenging arena, ghazal singing.Learning Urdu helped in getting the perfect pronunciation and diction,” says Joshi.Singer-composer Tejas Gambhir grew up listening to the legends. His soulful renditions of ghazals, sufi songs and qawwalis have earned him a huge following. His live, immersive “Mehfil-e-Sufi” and qawwali nights, says, Gambhir, are inspired by Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan and Ghulam Ali. He says Khan inspired him to present ghazals as qawwali numbers. “Nusrat sahab’s famous number Tumhein dil lagi bhool Jani paregi is actually a ghazal which he turned into a mesmerizing qawwali. So one kalam can be sung in different formats with the use of varried instruments,” says Gambhir. He places poet Krishna Behari Noor’s “Fursat ghamon se pana hai agar toh aao Noor/Sab ko karein salam chalo maikade chalein” among the ghazals he enjoyed singing.Maikada (tavern), sharab (wine) and saaqi (bartender) are strong metaphors frequently used in Sufi kalam and romantic ghazals. While the literal meaning of saaqi is the bartender, it could mean God too. Sometimes singers explain certain words during live performances,Many are “experimenting” and fusing with different genres in ghazals too. Singer-composer Prithvi Gandharv who became a household name with his participation in “Bandish Bandit”, a musical romantic drama web series, says new experiments are being done in the ghazal singing arena as well.“Jazz Ghazal is a genre gaining popularity today. Unlike the solo performances the past generations patronised in packed venues, now many singers sit on sofas accompanied by half a dozen instruments, including guitar on the stage,” says Gandharv.To some veterans, this fusion is nothing but “confusion”. “I hate words like experiment and fusion. Let ghazal remain ghazal. By blending sounds of different instruments and giving the ghazal mehfil the feel of a rock band, they are killing the soul of ghazal,” protests senior singer, composer and mentor Pandit Somesh Kumar Mathur whose recent creation Achcha Hai, comprising classical shairi of Mir, Ghalib, Momin and Jigar Muradabadi, is in the race for the 69th Grammy Awards to be announced in January 2027. Mathur adds that a singer like Asha Bhosle (he had collaborated with her on a ghazal album) lifted ghazal gaiki to dizzying heights even though she made a name as a playback singer.Despite distractions and short attention spans, the singers do bring the Gen Z to the mehfils. “I have noticed many youngsters busy with their mobile phones and suddenly waking during concerts if a good ghazal comes up,” says Joshi. “It is a challenge to keep a young crowd involved, but we are trying our best.”
Article Summary: Post--legends like Mehdi Hasan Jagjit Singh, Pankaj Udhas, pioneering couple Rajendra and Nina Mehta popular as “Musical MehtA’s”, the torch has been passed over to a bunch of young, energetic ghazal singers.

Article Title: Lyrical tribute to Meena Kumari in city next week
Article Text: Following Meena Kumari ’s death on March 31, 1972, her contemporary and close friend Nargis wrote a poignant open letter. Titled “Maut Mubarak Ho (congratulations on your death),” the letter published in now defunct Urdu magazine Shama, recalls Kumari once confiding in Nargis: “Baji (elder sister), resting is not in my destiny. I will rest just one time.”The legendary film actor Meena Kumari or Mehjabeen Bano (1933--1972) rests at Rahmatabad, the Shia cemetery at Mazgaon. And city-based playback singer Sanjeevni Bhelande will lead the legend’s commemoration by National Gallery of Modern Art, Fort with a free and non-commercial show on July 27.In a short life of 39, Kumari packed a panorama of events: forced by parents to become child artiste , solitude, romance, marriage with and separation from filmmaker Kamal Amrohi , stardom with classics like Sahab Biwi Aur Ghulam and Pakeezah, her battle with alcoholism-caused liver cirrhosis which eventually claimed her life.Some of these episodes from her eventful life feature in Bhelande’s show. “Meenaji’s photograph at an exhibition at NGMA drew me to to this great actor. I began researching her life. As I dug deep, a fascinating figure emerged. I decided to do a show combining anecdotes associated with some of the songs from her landmark films and the times which shaped her,” says Bhelande, famous for hit numbers like Chori chori nazrein mili and Nikamma kiya iss dilne in Vidhu Vinod Chopra’s film Kareeb.Giving context to some of the songs from Kumari’s films, celebrated as part of Hindi cinema’s golden age, Bhelande also discusses the sur and taal, their intrinsic qualities as well as reasons for their popularity.Take the song Ajeeb dastan hai yeh in the classic romantic drama Dil Apna Aur Preet Parai (1960). Penned by Shailendra and sung by Lata Mangeshkar , the song beautifully captures the unexplained tension and complex relationship between Dr. Sushil Verma (Raj Kumar) and nurse Karuna (Meena Kumari). “I quote Lataji on the show saying that this song is an honour to her own sur or musical notes,” says the singer.She also discusses the song Inhi logon ne... from Pakeezah (1972), Kumari’s final masterpiece. A poignant portrayal of the courtesan Sahibjaan (Meena Kumari), the film crystallised her status as Bollywood’s Tragedy Queen and the song Inhi logon ne...acquired became an emblem for the portrayal of courtesans in popular culture.“Though from the Sunni background, she was buried at Rahmatabad in Mazgaon according to her husband Kamal Amrohi’s wish. Amrohi too is buried beside her. I remember Shia scholar Maulana Abbas Rizvi talking fondly about her,” says businessman Javed Shroff.
Article Summary: Sanjeevni Bhelande will lead the legend’s commemoration by National Gallery of Modern Art, Fort with a free and non-commercial show on July 27. Kumari packed a panorama of events: forced by parents to become child artiste, solitude, romance, marriage with and separation from filmmaker Kamal Amrohi.

Article Title: ‘I will hug him tightly and perform an aarti’: Abhijeet Dipke’s parents express relief after weeks of anxiety
Article Text:
Parents expressed immense joy and relief following the successful campaign by Abhijeet Dipke.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Relief and celebration replaced months of anxiety for the parents of the Cockroach Janata Party ( CJP ) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday after the campaign spearheaded by him culminated in Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation."I will ask him to come home early. If he does not come, we will go and bring him back. I will hug him tightly and perform an aarti for him. The last time he was here, he did not allow me to do that, saying he was not some prominent person," said Abhijeet's mother, Anita Dipke, struggling to hold back her tears."I am extremely happy. His honesty has won. The support of the youth helped him, and he achieved a big victory," she said.Anita said she had remained anxious ever since her son returned to India and launched the agitation seeking Union education minister Pradhan's resignation over the NEET paper leak issue.She said she lost sleep after the CJP began its protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, news agency PTI reported."I was worried all the time. I had sleepless nights. Every morning, I was scared to even look at my phone, fearing I would see a disturbing video.I would immediately call his friends to ask if he was safe," Anita said.She said Abhijeet's friends repeatedly assured her that he would become emotional whenever he came to know about her worries and that they were always with him, taking care of him.Remembering the day the agitation began, Anita said she had cried out of fear and helplessness. "Today, the tears in my eyes are of happiness," she said.Calling Pradhan's resignation a "victory of the youth", Anita said thousands of youngsters had worked relentlessly to make the campaign successful.She, however, said she did not think her son would launch a political party and believed he would continue working in the social sector, PTI reported.Abhijeet's father, Bhagwanrao Dipke, said the family had been living in constant fear since his son floated the CJP despite having no political background."We were all worried when he took the political plunge. He went against my wishes. Nobody in our family had any political background," he said.The family had even appealed to Abhijeet not to return to India from the United States in June as they feared he could be arrested."We were so scared that during the initial days we left home and stayed in Konkan. We were under tremendous pressure. There were threats of physical harm to us," Bhagwanrao said.He said the stress had taken a severe toll on the family's health."We became so weak that we could barely stand. We were eating barely one roti a day. We could neither eat properly nor sleep. He was attacked twice during the agitation," Bhagwanrao said.Recalling the events of July 20, Bhagwanrao said seeing a police officer pull down Abhijeet's microphone reminded him of a battle scene from the film "Border"."I felt that if my Abhijeet fell into the hands of the police, he would not survive. By God's grace, he is safe. I honestly feel he should now come home and stay with us," he said.On Pradhan's resignation, Bhagwanrao said the Union minister had displayed "a big heart" by stepping down while asking students to concentrate on their education."This should not be seen as anybody's victory or defeat. Leaving such a high post requires a big heart. Even while resigning, he thought about the interests of students," he said.Describing his son as a well-educated person who had carefully planned the agitation before launching it, Bhagwanrao said he was uncertain about Abhijeet's next political move."He had earlier worked with (AAP leader) Arvind Kejriwal and has seen politics closely. I personally do not like politics, so I have no idea what he will do next. But I will be with him," Bhagwanrao said.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: Parents of CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke expressed joy and relief following the successful campaign by him. The campaign spearheaded by him culminated in Union minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation. His mother, Anita Dipke, said she had remained anxious ever since her son returned to India.

Article Title: CM Fadnavis says ‘satisfied’ with what he has been given; will keep Devendraji here in Maharashtra, says wife Amruta
Article Text:
Chief minister Fadnavis said there were two distinct strands within the agitation, one comprising students genuinely concerned about their future and another attempting to exploit the issue politically.

Kolhapur:

ji





Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis on Saturday brushed aside speculation about a possible induction into the Union cabinet, saying he was “satisfied” with his current responsibilities. His wife, Amruta Fadnavis , said she would not allow him to shift to New Delhi.The remarks came after the couple performed the official Mahapuja of Lord Vitthal and Goddess Rukmini at the Vitthal-Rukhmini temple on the occasion of Ashadhi Ekadashi. Later in the evening, Fadnavis left for New Delhi.More than 20 lakh warkari devotees thronged the temple town for the annual pilgrimage. This was the sixth time Devendra and Amruta Fadnavis performed the Ashadhi Ekadashi Mahapuja. Fadnavis had also attended the Kartiki Ekadashi Mahapuja twice while serving as deputy chief minister.When asked whether they would return next year to perform the ritual, Amruta initially said they would do so whether they are in Mumbai, Nagpur or Pandharpur. However, when specifically asked about speculation that Fadnavis may soon be moved to Delhi, she said, “I will also not let Devendramove to Delhi.”The comment came amid fresh political chatter after Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut said that Fadnavis could be considered for a role in the Union cabinet.“I feel that Devendra Fadnavis could replace Dharmendra Pradhan. He is a lawyer, he is educated and presents different subjects well. There has been discussion about Fadnavis going to Delhi and he could get the opportunity now,” Raut said.Speaking on the ongoing students’ agitation, Amruta Fadnavis said demonstrations were justified as long as they remained focused on the issue of examination paper leaks.“It was absolutely OK if the agitation had been restricted to the paper leak. Govt has been taking corrective measures in the background, and now we are seeing the results too,” she said.Chief minister Fadnavis said there were two distinct strands within the agitation, one comprising students genuinely concerned about their future and another attempting to exploit the issue politically.“Considering this situation, Sonam Wangchuk broke his fast; all his demands were accepted, and he also appealed to everyone to go ahead peacefully,” he said.Asked about the protest called by the Thackeray cousins in Mumbai on Sunday, Fadnavis said political motives appeared to be driving the mobilisation.“Everyone has the right in a democracy to speak their opinion. But I feel there is less possibility of this protest having any relation with the students. There is a greater possibility of efforts to establish themselves (the Thackerays) in politics again. Still our well-wishers are with them,” he said.Fadnavis also participated in the traditional Ashadhi Ekadashi celebrations, praying for the welfare of the state, good rainfall and prosperity for farmers as lakhs of devotees converged on Pandharpur for one of Maharashtra’s largest religious gatherings.
Article Summary: Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis brushed aside speculation about a possible induction into the Union cabinet, saying he was “satisfied’ with his current responsibilities. His wife, Amruta FadNavis, said she would not allow him to shift to New Delhi.

Article Title: 4 held for theft of 17 kg silver mask, cladding of Shivling at historic temple in Maharashtra's Khopoli
Article Text:
Khopoli police arrested four burglars for stealing silver items from a historic temple





NAVI MUMBAI: The Khopoli police in Raigad detected the burglary at the 18th century historic Shree Vireshwar temple, where 17 kg silver mask and silver cladding on Shivling was stolen on July 19 past midnight around 2 am, by arresting four accused burglars on Tuesday.The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe (36) and Vikas Agiwale (25), who were arrested from Shirur, Pune district and Dilip Jadhav (40) and Sakharam Gaikwad (40), who were arrested from Parner in Ahilyanagar district.The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust from the donations received from devotees.Sachin Hire, senior inspector of Khopoli said, "On July 19, the assistant priest at the temple identified as Kishore Shigwan (56) lodge a complaint that the silver mask and cladding on Shivling was stolen. The thieves had entered the temple by breaking the chain and lock of the rear gate, which always remained close as the devotees were allowed entry only from the front gate.""Upon checking CCTV camera footage at the temple, it was seen that four masked men had entered the sanctum sanctorum around 2 am and decamped with the silver mask and cladding on the Shivling. Subsequently, an FIR was registered under BNS sections for house tres-pass, theft in a dwelling house and joint criminal liability. "Inspector Hire said, "Multiple teams were formed to trace the gang of burglars.Using technical expertise and informer network, we zeroed-in on four history-sheeters. They were traced to Pune and Ahilyanagar district and gradually apprehended on Tuesday.""They have revealed the place where they have hidden the stolen silver mask and cladding. Accordingly, a police team will recover the stolen valuables. Previously, there are criminal cases of theft and robbery registered against the arrested accused in Ahilyanagar and Pune districts."
Article Summary: The 17 kg silver mask and cladding on the Shivling was adorned in 2023 for which the around Rs 28 lakhs expenses were borne by the temple's trust. The arrested accused are Amol Kasbe, Vikas Agiwale, Dilip Jadhav and Sakharam Gaikwad.

Article Title: Man booked for sexually assaulting and injuring stray dog in Navi Mumbai
Article Text:
Unidentified man booked for sexually assaulting female stray dog (Representative image generated using AI)





NAVI MUMBAI: A 31-year-old woman advocate, who is a dog lover, has registered an FIR at Ulwe police station against an unidentified man aged 30-35 years for allegedly sexually assaulting a female stray dog and causing injury to her private part.The incident occurred outside a tea shop on the ground floor in Siddhivinayak Platinum society in sector 23, Ulwe on Sunday around 11.45pm.Acting on a complaint by Advocate Gayatri Khanvilkar, a resident of the said building, the unidentified accused was booked under BNS section and Prevention of Cruelty to Animal.Adv Khanvilkar said, "As per my daily routine, on Sunday night, I went downstairs to feed the stray dogs loitering near our building. It was raining heavily and pitch darkness due to defunct streetlight poles.""I pucker whistled to call the dogs, when a female stray dog, who had delivered puppies last month, came out from behind a plastic table kept horizontally lying on the floor outside the closed tea shop next to the building's main gate. I could see a man hiding behind the table. I became suspicious and asked him what he was doing.""The man ran away semi-naked with his trouser and underwear in his hand.I chased him but taking advantage of the darkness amid heavy rains, he escaped towards the highway."She added, "I called my father downstairs after informing about the incident. We closely checked the dog and found her bleeding from private part. Also, there was human semen on the floor behind the table. I fed the dog and contacted a volunteer of an NGO Jeevan Foundation Yuva Sena, Animal Welfare Force in Kharghar.""I arranged a cab for the volunteer, who took the injured dog to Panvel Panchayat Samiti's Animal Husbandry department, opposite Panvel ST bus depot, where the government veterinarian confirmed sexual assault on the dog, who was treated for the injuries. Hence, I registered an FIR against the unidentified accused man for sexually assaulting the female stray dog and causing injury to her private part.""Our building's CCTV footage shows the accused man running away from the building, but just because the street lights were not working, his image was not clearly visible. We are retrieving more CCTV footages from other shops in our building for providing them to Ulwe police."PSI Rama Dhavare of Ulwe said, "After registering an FIR, the forensic team collected the human semen sample and hair strands from the crime scene. Once the accused is arrested, the DNA match will be the vital evidence in court for conviction of the accused."
Article Summary: The incident occurred outside a tea shop on the ground floor in Siddhivinayak Platinum society in sector 23, Ulwe on Sunday around 11.45pm. The unidentified accused was booked under BNS section and Prevention of Cruelty to Animal.

Article Title: 9 woman rescued from flesh trade in Taloja lodge, 3 accused held
Article Text:
The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.

NAVI MUMBAI: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit (AHTU) of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja and rescued nine women from the flesh trade on July 18. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters.Gajanan Kadam, senior inspector of AHTU said, "As per the information received about prostitution being carried out at Hotel Abode Inn Lodging and Boarding in Taloja, we set a trap by sending a decoy customer, whom the lodge manager provided a woman for sexual favour for Rs 3,000 that was accepted by one waiter. On the signal of the customer customer, we raided the lodge, where 9 women were kept for prostitution. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested for dragging the women into prostitution. An FIR was registered at Taloja police station against the three arrested accused Gowda, Pujari and Patil, who were booked relevant BNS sections and Prevention of Immoral Trafficking Act. The Panvel court remanded them to police custody till July 21. The rescued women were sent to women's shelter home as directed by the magistrate."
Article Summary: The Anti-Human Trafficking Unit of Navi Mumbai crime branch busted a prostitution racket at hotel-cum lodge in Taloja. The crime branch team arrested three accused including the lodge manager and two waiters. The lodge manager Balram Gowda, waiters Girish Pujari and Krishnaraj Patil were arrested.

Article Title: Truck driver arrested from Gujarat for killing fellow driver with iron rod over caste dispute in Maharashtra
Article Text:
Taloja police have caught a truck driver involved in the tragic murder of a fellow driver during a dispute fueled by caste discrimination (Representative image)

NAVI MUMBAI: Taloja police have arrested a 40-year-old truck driver who had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod in the truck parking lot of Nisha Transport company in Nitlas village near Taloja industrial area in Panvel taluka on July 14 early morning.The accused was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday, while he was escaping by train to his home town in UP.The arrested accused has been identified as Ramesh Kumar Yadav and the murder victim as Chandan Pandey, both hailing from UP.Sagar Nikam, PI (crime) of Taloja said, "The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP. The accused Yadav had fatally assaulted the victim Pandey as the latter being a Brahmin used to humiliate Yadav from OBC by treating him as inferior, as claimed by the accused Yadav."PI Nikam informed, "On Monday night, an argument has ensued between Pandey and Yadav in the parking lot over caste discrimination. As they quarrelled, the other truck drivers intervened and resolved the matter. On Tuesday around 5.30 am, again both of them quarrelled, when Yadav assaulted on Pandey's head with an iron rod that proved fatal.""Pandey escaped after threatening other truckers if they attempted to catch him. The security guard Mohammad Alam Hajif-ul Khan (58) informed the police. Pandey was rushed to Panvel sub-district hospital where he was declared brought dead. Subsequently, a murder case was registered against the accused Yadav. His photograph found in his parked truck was immediately circulated to the GRP and RPF at railway stations where multiple trains heading to UP halt.""On Friday, the Valsad GRP informed us that Yadav has been detained at Valsad railway station while he was travelling in an express train to escape to his hometown in UP. Our police team reached Valsad and arrested Yadav. The Panvel JMFC court has remanded Yadav to police custody untill July 21."
Article Summary: Ramesh Kumar Yadav, 40, was arrested from Valsad railway station, Gujarat on Friday. He had absconded after fatally assaulting a 45-year-old truck driver on his head with an iron rod. The murder was an outcome of the Pandey versus Yadav caste discrimination, especially in UP.

Article Title: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi
Article Text:
Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi (Representational Image)

NAVI MUMBAI: The Navi Mumbai crime branch unit-2 team has arrested a murder accused from Bhiwandi while conducting a parallel probe in the murder case registered at NRI Coastal police station on Friday after an unidentified man's body with head injuries was found on the pavement near D-Mart in sector 15, Belapur on Friday around 1 am.The arrested accused has been identified as Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.Anil Patil, senior inspector of crime branch unit-2 informed that, during the probe, when inquired with some rag pickers in the locality, we got an eye witness, who knew Ansari and had seen him assaulting Shaikh with a wooden stick on Thursday night as a quarrel broke out between them after they together consumed liquor near the pavement.The eye witness told that Ansari would pick up rags during day and would spend night where ever he found empty gala or incomplete under construction bldg in Belapur and his father resided in Bhiwandi.Using technical expertise and informer network Ansari was apprehended from Bhiwandi within 24 hours. Thereafter, the murder victim's identity was revealed by him.SPI Patil said, "Ansari claimed that Shaikh was habitual of abusing others after getting drunk. On Thursday night, after the liquor session, Shaikh turned violent without being provoked and attempted to assault him with an iron rod after pushing him to the ground. Hence, he confronted Shaikh by assaulting him with a wooden stick on his head. Seeing Shaikh bleeding profusely and fallen unconscious, he escaped to Bhiwandi. "
Article Summary: Rag picker's murder detected within 24 hours, accused arrested from Bhiwandi. Mohammad Irfan Mohammed Husain Ansari (36) and the murder victim as Salman Anwar Shaikh (27), a resident of Govandi. Both working as rag pickers for livelihood.

Article Title: Curated lifestyle exhibitions take over Pune this monsoon
Article Text:
Indoor curated fleas and exhibitions lined up ahead of the festive season

Pune





: With the monsoon in full swing and the festive season on the horizon, the city is witnessing a surge in indoor flea markets and curated lifestyle exhibitions. Organisers reported an enthusiastic turnout, particularly from micro-entrepreneurs, home-based businesses, and women-led brands looking to capitalise on the pre-festive shopping rush.Traditionally held outdoors, these markets are moving into more climate-controlled spaces. “This is the first time we are hosting indoor flea markets inside malls,” said Seema Dholi, organiser at Pune Flea. “We have launched 2–3 day exhibitions at Tribeca Mall and Aeromall, and this model will extend into our festive schedule later this year.”The optimism is shared by small-scale sellers. Dina Agarwal, who runs a handmade candle business, said her recent participation in a monsoon-themed cafe sale exceeded expectations.“The response was so good that we have already signed up for exhibitions in September,” she added.Major community platforms are also seeing a spike in demand. Sonia Agarwal Konjeti, founder of PULA (Pune Ladies), noted that the demand for stall space is currently outpacing supply. “We have four exhibitions lined up in the run-up to Diwali . Our August event is already sold out. Most of our sellers are local, covering everything from home décor and gifting to gourmet food,” she said.The vibrancy of the Pune market is also attracting talent from neighbouring districts. Payal J, a creator from Satara, has travelled to the city specifically for the season. “I’ve had a great response here in the past. This year, I’ve prepared specialised resin Rakhi trays and diyas for the upcoming festivals,” she said.Beyond malls and convention centers, local cafes—particularly in areas like NIBM and Aundh—are transforming into community hubs. Many are hosting weekend farmers’ markets and workshops alongside flea stalls to create a “lively, boutique atmosphere,” according to one NIBM-based cafe manager.For shoppers, these curated markets offer a break from mass-produced retail. “I recently visited a flea at a local cafe and found unique handicrafts I hadn’t seen elsewhere,” said Ria Ghatge, an Aundh resident. “I picked up hand-painted ceramics and coasters, and I definitely plan to hit more exhibitions as Diwali approaches to finish my gift shopping.”
Article Summary: Pune is witnessing a surge in indoor flea markets and curated lifestyle exhibitions. Organisers report an enthusiastic turnout, particularly from micro- entrepreneurs, home-based businesses, and women-led brands. For shoppers, these curated markets offer a break from mass-produced retail.

Article Title: Minor killed over suspected love affair; one arrested, juvenile detained in Pune
Article Text:
Pune:





A 17-year-old boy was assaulted to death by a 20-year-old man and his minor accomplice at Phursungi on Saturday morning on the suspicion that the deceased was having an affiar with a woman from Yewalewadi near Kondhwa.Phursungi police arrested the 20-year-old man from Kondhwa and have detained his minor accomplice later on Saturday afternoon. Article Title: IIT Madras counsels parents, sensitises them to stress endured by BTech freshers
Article Text:
To reduce stress to BTech students

Chennai:





To sensitise parents not to put extra pressure on their wards, IIT Madras on Saturday conducted a separate counselling session for parents of BTech students who joined the institute this year. This year, the counselling to parents had two former students explaining the expectations of students from their parents.Professors, psychiatrists and counsellors explained the mental health problems and doubts that were unique to IIT students.A mental health survey among the BTech students last year found that up to 13% of freshers entering IIT Madras have stress-related issues. The sessions were aimed at enlightening the parents about the pressures their wards might face while studying in IIT, including about grades, internships and job offers, and how parents can play a supportive role in the academic journey.“In IIT, everybody in the class is a top ranker. They are all exactly the same. We dont give ranks, we only give relative grading. It can be very demoralising if parents compare their scores or grades with past performance. Students’ own expectation will put them under pressure. Parents should moderate their expectations,” said professor Prathap Haridoss, dean (academics), IIT Madras.He asked parents to pay attention to whether their kids were sleeping well, eating well and to their social life, including friends inside the campus.He also told parents to enquire if a student misses classes in a row.“The teaching in schools and IIT is completely different, where students in IITs have to study on their own. Students tend to take time to adjust to the new way of learning. All students may not get the Day 1 jobs and growth takes time,” said professor Sathyanarayana N Gummadi, dean of students, IIT Madras.He also highlighted the successful alumni who chose different career paths, including civil services, entrepreneurship and academics.IIT Madras alumni Degala Chaitanya Kumar and Avinash Abhishek shared their experiences. Avinash Abhishek said the comforting words from his mother helped him to bag a job offer in his last campus interview.Two IFS officers from Karnataka, Biswajit Mishra and Saswati Mishra, and parents of a final-year student shared how one of their daughters struggled to cope with the academics and the timely help from the institute helped her to continue in IIT.Dr Yamini Kannappan, consultant psychiatrist from Kauvery Hospital, asked the parents to identify the early signs of distress. S Srividya, chief psychologist from Myndwell, spoke about how different addictions could impact students during the academic programme.Ram Babu, a veteran from the Indian Air Force from Guntur in Andhra Pradesh, had several concerns about the well-being of his kid who joined BTech this year at IIT Madras. After attending a three-hour-long counselling session for parents, he said he understood the pressures of studying in IIT and will try not to put extra pressure.
Article Summary: A mental health survey among the BTech students last year found that up to 13% of freshers entering IIT Madras have stress-related issues. This year, the counselling to parents had two former students explaining the expectations of students from their parents.

Article Title: E-challan blunder: Non-functional two-wheeler slapped with 249 wrongful traffic fines to the tune of Rs 3 lakh in Coimbatore
Article Text:
Representative image





COIMBATORE: A non-functional two-wheeler bearing the registration number TN 37 AF 4170 has accumulated 249 pending traffic challans to the tune of more than Rs 3 lakh on the official Parivahan portal.A cross-check of the govt portal revealed a systemic breakdown between 2019 and May 2026. Dozens of traffic violation fines belonging to completely different vehicles were systematically dumped on this single, non-operational bike. The offences, such as riding motorcycles without helmet, rash driving, triple riding, pillion rider without helmet and even drunk driving cases, were transferred to this particular vehicle.The blunder exposes severe flaws in the police's e-challan verification process. In several cases, uploaded evidence photos clearly capture other motorcycles committing offences such as "no parking," yet the fines were slapped on the owners of uninvolved vehicles.B Annammal of Podanur shared her ordeal after receiving a Rs 500 fine. "When I downloaded the challan, my scooter was nowhere in the frame; a completely different bike was parked in the restricted zone," she said."The personnel mistyped my registration number, leaving me penalised for a crime I never committed while the actual violator walked away scot-free."When contacted, Coimbatore city police commissioner N Kannan stated that he was unaware of the issue but promised a thorough inquiry. "We need to determine if this stems from a technical glitch or human error," Kannan said. "If it is a man-made error, we will investigate whether it was done knowingly or unknowingly. Severe action will be taken if any malpractices are uncovered."S S Maheswaran, deputy commissioner of police (traffic), Coimbatore city, stated that they would verify with the technical team and try to resolve the issue.
Article Summary: A non-functional two-wheeler bearing the registration number TN 37 AF 4170 has accumulated 249 pending traffic challans. The offences, such as riding motorcycles without helmet, rash driving, triple riding, pillion rider without helmet and even drunk driving cases, were transferred to this particular vehicle. The blunder exposes severe flaws in the police's e-challan verification process.

Article Title: Quote of the Day by Marcus Aurelius, the Roman emperor who inspired Gladiator: "You have power over your mind, not outside events..."
Article Text:
Image: Getty Images

Quote of the Day by Marcus Aurelius: "You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realise this, and you will find strength."

Who was Marcus Aurelius?

The Stoic philosophy behind the quote



Why the quote remains relevant today



Lessons readers can apply in daily life

A timeless reminder from ancient Rome

Many people recognise Marcus Aurelius as the wise Roman emperor whose fictionalised character inspired Ridley Scott's Gladiator. Yet long before Hollywood brought ancient Rome to the big screen, Marcus Aurelius had earned a place in history as one of the greatest Stoic philosophers and one of Rome's most respected rulers. His private writings, later compiled as Meditations, continue to inspire millions around the world with their timeless reflections on resilience, discipline and inner peace. Among his most enduring observations is: "You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realise this, and you will find strength." Although written nearly 2,000 years ago, the quote remains remarkably relevant in a world shaped by uncertainty, social media pressures and constant change.At its heart, Marcus Aurelius' quote is a reminder that while people cannot control everything that happens around them, they can control how they respond. Life is full of unexpected challenges, from personal disappointments and workplace stress to global events beyond anyone's influence. According to Stoic philosophy, peace comes not from trying to change external circumstances but from mastering one's own thoughts and reactions.The second part of the quote, "Realise this, and you will find strength," explains where genuine resilience comes from. Strength is not measured by physical power or status but by emotional stability and the ability to remain calm when circumstances become difficult.Marcus Aurelius ruled the Roman Empire from AD 161 until his death in AD 180. He is remembered as the last of Rome's "Five Good Emperors" and led the empire during a period marked by wars, political challenges and outbreaks of disease. Despite carrying enormous responsibilities, he found time to write personal reflections that would later become Meditations, one of history's most influential philosophical works.Unlike books written for publication, Meditations was intended as a private journal. Marcus Aurelius used it to remind himself how to live with integrity, patience and humility. The honesty of these writings has allowed readers across centuries to relate to his struggles and wisdom.Although Gladiator introduced Marcus Aurelius to modern audiences, the film took considerable creative liberties. In reality, he was not murdered by his son Commodus, as portrayed in the movie. Historians believe he died of illness while leading military campaigns near the empire's northern frontier.Marcus Aurelius belonged to the Stoic school of philosophy, which taught that happiness depends more on character than on external success. Stoicism encourages individuals to focus only on what lies within their control while accepting everything else with courage and wisdom.This philosophy divides life into two categories. The first includes things people can influence, such as their decisions, attitudes, values and actions. The second includes everything beyond their control, including other people's behaviour, the weather, economic conditions and unexpected setbacks.Marcus Aurelius believed much of human suffering comes from confusing these two categories. People often exhaust themselves trying to control circumstances they cannot change instead of improving the one thing they truly possess: their own mind.Modern life presents countless situations that reinforce Marcus Aurelius' advice. People worry about social media opinions, office politics, financial uncertainty or events unfolding across the world. While these concerns are understandable, obsessing over them rarely changes the outcome.The quote encourages a healthier approach. Rather than allowing outside events to dictate emotions, individuals can choose patience, rational thinking and self-control. This mindset often leads to better decision-making because reactions are guided by reason instead of fear or anger.Psychologists also recognise that focusing on controllable actions helps reduce stress and anxiety. Although Marcus Aurelius lived nearly two millennia before modern psychology emerged, his observations closely resemble concepts used today in cognitive behavioural therapy, which teaches people to challenge unhelpful thoughts and focus on constructive responses.Marcus Aurelius' wisdom is practical rather than abstract. The quote can be applied in everyday situations.When criticism arises, people cannot always control what others say, but they can choose whether to let those words define them. When plans fail, they cannot rewrite the past, but they can decide how to move forward. During periods of uncertainty, they cannot predict every outcome, but they can prepare thoughtfully and respond calmly.This perspective does not encourage ignoring problems or avoiding responsibility. Instead, it reminds people to invest their energy where it can make a meaningful difference. By concentrating on personal growth, discipline and thoughtful action, individuals often become more resilient and effective.Nearly 2,000 years after Marcus Aurelius wrote Meditations, his reflections continue to influence readers ranging from business leaders and athletes to military officers and students. His ideas have survived because they address universal human experiences that remain unchanged despite technological and social progress.The quote, "You have power over your mind, not outside events. Realise this, and you will find strength," captures one of Stoicism's central lessons: lasting strength begins within. External circumstances will always change, but a disciplined mind can remain steady through success and failure alike.Whether readers first encountered Marcus Aurelius through history books, philosophy or Gladiator, his words continue to offer practical guidance for navigating modern life. In an age filled with distractions, uncertainty and constant noise, his reminder to focus on what truly lies within our control is as valuable today as it was in ancient Rome.
Article Summary: Marcus Aurelius ruled the Roman Empire from AD 161 until his death in AD 180. He is remembered as the last of Rome's "Five Good Emperors" Despite carrying enormous responsibilities, he found time to write personal reflections that would later become Meditations, one of history's most influential philosophical works.
